clue.text: Start off voyage and see an edible shellfish and long kipper

indicators.note: the start of the word is taken off, so its first letter goes

parts.note: a trip is a voyage or journey
V is short for vide, Latin for 'see', as in cross-references
taken as written
a winkle is a small edible sea snail

explanation.surface: Instructions for a seaside outing: set off on a trip, eat shellfish, then have a long nap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start off' removes the first letter of TRIP, leaving RIP. 'Kipper' here is someone who kips (sleeps), not the smoked fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The folk-tale character slept for twenty years, so he is the archetypal long sleeper, a 'kipper' in the sense of one who kips.

clue.text: Ask the French what will take place during holiday

indicators.note: taking place during something means sitting within it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a rest is a break, a holiday
que is French for 'what'

explanation.surface: Asking a French speaker what will happen while on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the French' tells you to translate the next word into French. 'will take place during' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To request is to ask for something, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Stuck-up pair meeting another stuck-up pair

parts.note: a duo is a pair

indicators.note: in a down clue stuck up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a duo is a pair

explanation.surface: A snobbish couple meeting another snobbish couple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuck-up' is both the definition and, the second time, the reversal of DUO to OUD in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Proud can mean haughty or arrogant, as well as sticking out from a surface.

clue.text: Story told whose beginning is a disgrace

parts.note: a 'story' spoken is a storey, and the storey at a building's bottom, where it begins, is the basement

explanation.surface: A tale whose opening is an embarrassment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Story' is a homophone of storey, a building's floor; the lowest one is the basement, and A comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Abasement is humiliation or degradation, a state of disgrace.

clue.text: Perverse desire, mainly, to get loudly drunk

indicators.note: mainly means most of the word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: will is desire or wish

indicators.note: loudly says the word is heard, giving a different spelling that sounds the same

parts.note: full is informal for drunk

explanation.surface: A contrary urge to get noisily drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mainly' trims WILL to WIL; 'loudly' turns FULL into the sound-alike ending FUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilful means obstinately self-willed, contrary, which is a sense of perverse.

clue.text: Close to agreement over what last drink might be

parts.note: nigh means near, close to

indicators.note: in a down answer over means the word is flipped to read upwards

parts.note: a pact is an agreement

explanation.surface: Nearly agreeing on what to have for a final drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses PACT to TCAP below NIGH.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightcap is the drink taken before bed, typically the last of the evening.

clue.text: Superior pork pie, for instance, that's eaten

indicators.note: something eaten goes inside, so one piece is swallowed by another

parts.note: pork pie (porky) is British rhyming slang for a lie
eg abbreviates exempli gratia, for instance

explanation.surface: A top-quality pork pie, say, being eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: Pork pie (often 'porky') is Cockney rhyming slang: pork pie rhymes with lie. 'that's eaten' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A liege is a feudal lord, the superior to whom vassals owe allegiance.

clue.text: Works to provide backing for leading players

definitions.text: Works to provide backing for leading players

parts.words: Works to provide backing for leading players
parts.note: pieces of music in which an orchestra accompanies a featured soloist, the leading player

explanation.surface: Efforts to finance the star members of a team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' suggests financial support; it is orchestral accompaniment behind soloists.
explanation.definitionFit: Concertos are compositions for soloist with orchestral accompaniment, so works backing the leading player.

clue.text: Doctor blamed for pandemonium

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are altered

explanation.surface: A doctor gets blamed for chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a noun but is the verb for tampering.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedlam, from the old London asylum, means uproar and confusion.

clue.text: One repeating aloud the amount allowed

indicators.note: aloud says the words are heard rather than read, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: someone who repeats another's words is a quoter

explanation.surface: Someone reciting out loud the allowance they have been given.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR copy carries a stray apostrophe before 'repeating'; the page has none. In non-rhotic speech the two words sound identical.
explanation.definitionFit: A quota is a fixed share or ration permitted to someone, exactly an allowed amount.

clue.text: Member to support European dismissed like this?

parts.note: a leg is a limb, a member of the body
to be for something is to support it

explanation.surface: A politician backing a European cause gets thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: LEG BEFORE (wicket) is a way a batsman is given out in cricket, when the ball would have hit the stumps but struck the leg; 'Member' looks like a club or parliament member.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a batsman can be dismissed leg before wicket, so the phrase describes a manner of being out.

clue.text: Latest issue bound to have affected Ulster

parts.note: a bound is a limit or boundary, an end

indicators.note: affected means altered or disturbed, so the letters of the following word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Bound to change Northern Ireland's politics, the newest development has arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to have affected' signals the anagram of Ulster, which follows the synonym for bound.
explanation.definitionFit: The final outcome of a process is its latest issue, issue meaning result or consequence.

clue.text: So-called extra large cap

indicators.note: so-called signals the clue words are named as they are spoken

parts.note: XL is the clothing-size abbreviation for extra large

explanation.surface: A label on a cap reading extra large.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, the letters X L give the sound of the answer. 'Cap' is the verb meaning outdo, not the hat.
explanation.definitionFit: To cap something is to top or surpass it, which is what it means to outdo others.

clue.text: Watch teacher giving correct marks

definitions.meaning: slang for a watch or clock, from the sound it makes
someone putting check marks against right answers

explanation.definitionFit: Ticker is slang for a timepiece, and also literally one who ticks answers correct.

clue.text: After May, sign seen in holiday resort

indicators.note: after puts the sign behind the first word

parts.note: can means may, be permitted
Aries is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: Once May comes, a sign appears at a holiday destination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'May' looks like the month but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The Canary Islands, or Canaries, are a popular holiday destination off Africa.

clue.text: Girl who's into grass gets pot plant

indicators.note: into places the girl's name inside the grass

parts.note: marram is a coarse grass that binds sand dunes
Jo is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl wandering into the grass finds a plant in a pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pot' suggests a houseplant, but pot marjoram is the herb's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Pot marjoram is a culinary herb, so the herb is literally a 'pot' plant.

clue.text: Petty bureaucrat's problems with old PM after loss of leadership

parts.note: a job can be a difficult task, a problem

indicators.note: loss of leadership means the first letter, the leader, is removed

parts.note: Lord North was British Prime Minister 1770-82

explanation.surface: An official's difficulties with a former PM once he is no longer leader.
explanation.walkthrough: NORTH loses its head to give ORTH. The 's of the definition stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A jobsworth is a minor official who sticks rigidly to rules, i.e. a petty bureaucrat.

clue.text: A lot of letters, say, about abandoning principles

parts.note: the post is the mail, a batch of letters

indicators.note: about means the letters are turned around in some way, rearranged

explanation.surface: Lots of correspondence, so to speak, concerning giving up beliefs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges SAY to ASY.
explanation.definitionFit: Apostasy is the renunciation of a belief or principle once held.

clue.text: Monument, exactly right one, put back in church

indicators.note: in puts the reversed letters inside the church abbreviation
put back means the words are turned round to run backwards

parts.note: pat means exactly right, perfectly apt
taken as written

explanation.surface: A memorial that is perfectly fitting, returned to its place in the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put back' turns the two words together, giving ENOTAP; 'in' puts that inside the church abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A cenotaph is a war memorial honouring the dead buried elsewhere, a type of monument.

clue.text: Project given gold star

parts.note: to cast is to throw or project
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A scheme awarded a gold star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Project' is the verb, not a scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: Castor is a bright star in the constellation Gemini.

clue.text: Musician starting off by only improvising simple tune

indicators.note: starting says take the starting letter of each word that follows

explanation.surface: A player begins by just improvising a simple melody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starting off' reads as one phrase, but 'off' is the first word whose initial is taken.
explanation.definitionFit: An oboist plays the oboe, so is a kind of musician.

clue.text: The cloth's words uplifted priest

parts.note: a text is a body of words

indicators.note: in a down answer uplifted means the word is read upwards

parts.note: Eli is the priest in the Bible who brought up Samuel

explanation.surface: The clergy's words lifted up a priest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The cloth' suggests the clergy, but means fabric; its 's is 'is'. 'uplifted' reverses ELI to ILE.
explanation.definitionFit: A textile is any woven fabric, a cloth.

clue.text: He's got home very recently

parts.note: just means only a moment ago
in means at home

explanation.surface: Someone has only just arrived home.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is just 'He' with 's as 'is'; JUST IN also means got home very recently.
explanation.definitionFit: Justin is a man's name, so the answer is a 'he'.

clue.text: Frenchman bows, turning to leave in a hurry

indicators.note: turning means the word is turned round to read backwards

parts.note: arcs are bow shapes, curves
M is short for Monsieur, a French title for a man

explanation.surface: A Frenchman bowing politely and then rushing away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bows' looks like the gesture, but it is curved shapes; 'turning' reverses ARCS.
explanation.definitionFit: Scram is slang meaning go away quickly, i.e. to leave in a hurry.

clue.text: TV and press journalist aboard train going North

indicators.note: aboard places one piece inside another, as on a vehicle
in a down answer going north means read upwards

parts.note: to train a gun is to aim it
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter on a northbound train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going North' reverses, making MIA, since this is a down entry. 'Train' is the verb, not the railway.
explanation.definitionFit: The media are the mass-communication outlets, television and the press.

clue.text: Speaker on phone making protest before fight

indicators.note: before puts the protest ahead of the fight in the answer

parts.note: to squawk is to complain loudly
to box is to fight with fists

explanation.surface: Someone on the phone complaining before a brawl breaks out.
explanation.definitionFit: A squawk box is an informal name for a loudspeaker or intercom, such as on a telephone system.

clue.text: Book bishop dropped in bad temper

indicators.note: dropped in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: bile is irritability or bad temper
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop drops a book in a fit of anger.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bible is the Christian scripture, the Book par excellence.

clue.text: Advert for new sort of financial licence

indicators.note: new sort of says the letters are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An advertisement for a new kind of financial permit.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is both words 'Advert for'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank overdraft is permission to borrow beyond one's balance, a licence to spend money not held.

clue.text: Pan-Arab bid to imprison religious leader

indicators.note: to imprison means the answer is held within the letters of these words

explanation.surface: A pan-Arab attempt to jail a cleric.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbi is a Jewish scholar and teacher who leads a congregation, a religious leader.

clue.text: Attractive, yet one has unconventional look

indicators.note: unconventional means arranged in an unusual way, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: an eye is a look, as in 'cast an eye over'

explanation.surface: Someone attractive, though with an unusual appearance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unconventional' rearranges three clue words into EASYONTHE. 'Look' gives the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pleasant to look at is attractive, an idiom for good-looking.
